engrave.dxf_note: DXF has no fill attribute: the engraved art is closed polylines on layer ENGRAVE, so set that layer to fill / raster in the laser software.
conventions: Cuts are kerf-offset; engraving is not.
Engraving stays at least 0.35 mm from every cut.
Parts with art lie outside face up. Parts flagged 'flipped' are mirrored in the cut + engrave files for this; the art is not mirrored. Never flip a part to engrave a second side.
Parts without art lie inside face up and carry gray joint labels: the same number on the two edges that meet.
The drawer faceplate glue-up lines are in the cut + labels files only.

order: Cut the coupon first, on a scrap of your real plywood.
Measure the kerf square, pick the kerf file set that matches, and try the joints.
Measure the plywood thickness with calipers or from the slot gauge.

features.measure: outside width of the cut square, with calipers
features.then: Use the file set whose kerf is closest to the number you measured.

features.reading: the narrowest slot your plywood slides into without force
features.formula: thickness is about drawn width + kerf, rounded to 0.05
features.ticks: the marked coupon has i engraved ticks above slot i (1 = 2.8 mm); on the plain coupon the slots run from the narrowest to the widest in a row: count them in order
features.then: Pick the thickness set (2.8 ... 3.5 mm) nearest your plywood.

features.formula: cut hole = drawn diameter + kerf; the box wants a 5.65 mm hole for a 6.0 mm magnet
features.reading: the hole a 6 x 2 mm magnet pushes into with firm finger pressure and stays in
features.then: If that is the smallest hole, the plywood's hole is running big: nothing to change in the box files, but use a drop of glue. If the largest hole is still tight, the hole is running small: file or ream the 4 magnet holes.

features.identify: the pairs differ in size: the smallest pair is the diode set, the middle one CO2, the largest Ponoko; the marked coupon also has 1, 2 or 3 engraved ticks on both pieces of a pair
features.reading: press each finger piece into the hole piece of the same size
features.right: goes together with firm hand pressure, no gap, no rattle
features.tight_along_the_finger: tight when sliding along the length of the fingers: your kerf is smaller than that set assumes; use the next smaller kerf set
features.loose_along_the_finger: loose or rattling: your kerf is larger; use the next larger kerf set
features.tight_through_the_slot: the fingers will not go through the plywood thickness of the slot: your plywood is thicker than the set; use the next thickness

features.reading: slide the lid strip into the slot block
features.right: slides freely with a little vertical play (about 1.2 mm total)
